Category C training

Practical training for rigid lorries over 3.5 tonnes. This page explains who the course is for, what you can drive and how the training works.

Enquire about Category CCall 01632 960960

Who Category C is for

Drivers who want to move up from a car licence to a rigid lorry over 3.5 tonnes. You will usually need a category B car licence, and the medical and theory steps sit alongside the practical training.

If you already hold Category C and need a trailer, seeCategory C+E training.

What you can drive

Category C is the rigid lorry licence. It covers goods vehicles over 3.5 tonnes maximum authorised mass that are not articulated.

  • Rigid goods vehicles such as box wagons, tippers, flatbeds and similar lorries
  • Not an articulated lorry or a drawbar combination. That is Category C+E

You train in our own rigid training lorry.

Eligibility and prerequisites

General guidance only. We check the licence you hold when you enquire.

  • A category B car licence is the usual starting point
  • A medical assessment is normally needed before a lorry practical test
  • Theory tests go alongside your time in the vehicle
  • Paid driving work can also require Driver CPC, which is separate from the Category C licence
  • Age and medical rules depend on the person and the work, so this page can't confirm whether you qualify. We check when you enquire

Paid work may also involve Driver CPC. That is a separate qualification.

What training includes

  • Getting to know a rigid goods vehicle
  • Reversing and manoeuvres in the yard
  • On-road driving
  • Guidance on what the practical test involves

How the course works

Four steps, from your first enquiry to the practical test.

  1. Enquire about Category C

    Tell us you want to drive a rigid lorry, and how you'd like us to get in touch.

  2. We check your licence

    We look at the licence you hold and explain the medical and theory steps.

  3. Train in the vehicle

    Practical sessions cover getting to know the lorry, manoeuvres and road driving.

  4. Prepare for the practical test

    We explain how the test is booked and what to expect on the day.

How long it takes

How long training takes depends on the licence you already hold, your driving experience and how the sessions are arranged. We agree a plan with you when you enquire, rather than quoting a standard length.

Price and quotes

We don't publish a fixed price list, because the right training depends on the licence you hold and how much practice you need. Ask for a quote for the course you want. Medical, theory test and practical test fees are separate costs, and we explain them when we quote.

Common questions

What does Category C allow me to drive?

Rigid goods vehicles over 3.5 tonnes. It doesn't cover an articulated lorry or a drawbar trailer. That is Category C+E.

What do I need before practical training?

A car licence is the usual starting point, and a medical assessment and theory tests normally go alongside the practical training. We check your licence when you enquire.

How long does Category C take?

It depends on the licence you hold, your driving experience and how the days are arranged. We agree a plan with you when you enquire.

How much does Category C cost?

Ask us for a quote. Medical, theory test and practical test fees are separate costs, and we explain them when we quote.
